notes:
Background: SkyForge builds an IDE copilot used internally by >10k engineers and as a hosted add-on. Primary constraint: ultra-low latency (first-token <50ms for inline completions) and predictable per-seat economics. They currently run a mix of public cloud-hosted services and a private VPC for sensitive repos.

Customer objectives / asks: 
- Low-latency streaming inside VS Code plugin (proactive completion + on-demand whole-file refactors).
- Model/version pinning per team (can't accept automatic rollout without approval).
- Significant cost pressure: CFO expects per-seat inference OPEX to be predictable (target $4–6 active seat/month across bulk usage).
- Wants to explore aggressive quantization + distilled model variants for non-sensitive corp code, while keeping higher-precision model in VPC for private repos.

Technical notes from PoC: 
- PoC scope: measure tradeoffs between int8/awq quantized variants vs fp16 on A100; test prefix KV caching for common code patterns (boilerplate + imports).
- Early results (03/01 baseline): streaming FTT (first token time) 38ms using small optimized model on dedicated pool; fp16 on larger model ~70–90ms.
- Caching observed 2x token-cost reduction for repeated prefixes (monorepo templates).
- Major ask: per-seat throttling + burst policies so CI bots don't drive up per-seat unit costs.

Security & compliance: 
- Requires SSO/SAML, audit logs forwarded to their Splunk, and KMS integration for key wrapping. Data residency: EU dev teams must keep code and logs in eu-1 region; legal wants explicit retention controls.

Commercial / economics: 
- They are highly sensitive to token-based pricing but are open to per-seat blended models if Redwood can guarantee unit economics via caching/quantization profiles.
- Suggested proposal: base dedicated reservation for baseline capacity + overage priced with aggressive batching and caching discounts.

Quotes / voice notes: 
- "If latency creeps above 50ms for inline, adoption nose-dives" — Head of Developer Productivity.
- "We need predictable monthly line-item, not surprise token bills." — VP Finance.

Next steps (short): 
- Run quantization sweep (int8/awq) across 3 representative models; produce quality regression matrix by 2026-03-20.
- Deliver per-seat cost model scenarios (hosted vs dedicated vs private) by 2026-03-18.
- Legal to review data residency SLA; Redwood to provide draft by 2026-03-12.

Notes on blockers: 
- Budget sign-off pending Q2 procurement cycle.
- SAML integration window: engineering sprint conflict during mid-March.
